name: A Midsummer Night’s Dream
kicker: Shakespeare’s fairy comedy · A love potion mixes up two Athenian couples
briefing: Deep in a forest outside Athens, the fairy king Oberon and his queen Titania are in the middle of a marriage spat, and the mischievous sprite Puck is about to make it much worse. A magic flower meant to fix one couple’s love life ends up on the wrong eyelids, a boastful weaver named Bottom is given a donkey’s head, and everyone falls for the wrong person. _A Midsummer Night’s Dream_ is one of Shakespeare’s most performed comedies.

qb.tip: Only 2 hits at Middle School/Easy High School, so Regular HS tossups were added. One 2023 SITH tossup whose real answer was “dreams” (which merely accepted this title as an alternate) was skipped — it’s not really about this play.

sample.note: 6 real QBReader tossups (2 Middle School/Easy High School + 4 Regular High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: This play’s trickster sprite boasts that he can disguise himself as “a roasted crab” or a “three-foot stool” to play pranks on old women. Later, that same character smears a magic flower’s juice on the wrong Athenian’s eyelids, making him fall for the wrong woman.
tossups.r: A weaver named Nick Bottom is given a donkey’s head after rehearsing a play about Pyramus and Thisbe with his fellow “rude mechanicals.” For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy in which Puck’s mischief confuses two pairs of young lovers.

tossups.p: In one speech, a character claims that “the lunatic, the lover, and the poet are of imagination all compact.” That same character, the Duke of Athens, presides over the wedding that frames this play’s action.
tossups.r: In the forest outside his city, four young Athenians get tangled up after the fairy Puck mistakenly enchants the wrong man’s eyes with a love potion, and a weaver named Bottom is transformed so that he has a donkey’s head. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy featuring the fairy king Oberon and his queen Titania.

tossups.p: This play’s final speech begs the audience’s pardon, beginning “If we shadows have offended, think but this, and all is mended.” Earlier, the same speaker gleefully says, “Lord, what fools these mortals be!” as the enchanted Athenian lovers approach.
tossups.r: That mischievous fairy, Puck, had put a love potion on Lysander’s eyes, and Oberon had enchanted Demetrius’s, so both men chased Helena instead of Hermia. A weaver named Nick Bottom is given a donkey’s head while rehearsing a play with his fellow “rude mechanicals.” For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy set partly in an enchanted forest.

tossups.p: One character promises, “I go, I go; look how I go, swifter than arrow from the Tartar’s bow,” before carrying out a fairy king’s orders. That king, Oberon, wants the juice of a magic flower applied to his queen Titania’s eyes so she will fall for the first creature she sees.
tossups.r: That creature turns out to be Nick Bottom, a weaver whose head has just been turned into a donkey’s. Meanwhile, four young Athenians get hopelessly confused after the same potion is applied to the wrong pair of eyes. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy featuring the trickster sprite Puck.

tossups.p: During the mechanicals’ performance, the actor playing a lion assures the audience that he is really just Snug the joiner. Other members of that acting troupe play a wall and the moonlight in the same production.
tossups.r: Led by Peter Quince, the “rude mechanicals” perform the tragedy of Pyramus and Thisbe at a royal wedding. Earlier, in the forest, Puck’s love-potion mix-up leaves Helena pursued by both Lysander and Demetrius. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy in which weaver Nick Bottom is transformed with a donkey’s head.

tossups.p: Early in this play, a father demands that Athenian law be used to punish his daughter for refusing an arranged marriage; unless she obeys, she faces death or life in a convent. That daughter, Hermia, flees into the forest with her true love instead.
tossups.r: There, the fairy king Oberon orders Puck to use a magic flower’s juice to fix a mortal’s love troubles, but Puck enchants the wrong young man, making both Athenian suitors chase Helena. A weaver named Bottom is given a donkey’s head. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy featuring the fairy queen Titania.

tossups.p: Before this play begins, one character had abandoned his engagement to Helena after falling for her friend Hermia instead, which is why Helena now chases him into the forest. There, the fairy Puck’s meddling with a magic potion only deepens the confusion between the two couples.
tossups.r: Meanwhile, the fairy king Oberon wants to use the same flower’s juice to punish his queen Titania, who ends up falling in love with a donkey-headed weaver. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy that ends with a triple wedding in Athens.

tossups.p: This play’s fairy queen commands servants named Peaseblossom, Cobweb, Moth, and Mustardseed. She is tricked by her husband Oberon into falling in love with a weaver whose head has been turned into a donkey’s.
tossups.r: That weaver, Nick Bottom, had been rehearsing a tragedy about Pyramus and Thisbe with his fellow “rude mechanicals” when Puck transformed him. Meanwhile, four young Athenians get mixed up by the same magic flower. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy featuring the fairy queen Titania.

tossups.p: This play’s fairy king wants to win custody of a changeling Indian boy away from his wife, so he sends his servant to fetch a magic flower called “love-in-idleness.” That servant, Puck, fetches the flower, whose juice soon causes trouble far beyond the fairy queen.
tossups.r: Puck accidentally enchants Lysander instead of Demetrius, making both young men chase Helena through the forest, and he also gives a weaver named Bottom the head of a donkey. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy in which the fairy king Oberon and queen Titania feud over a changeling boy.

tossups.p: Scholars think Shakespeare wrote this comedy around 1595, possibly for an aristocratic wedding celebration, and its earliest printed text, a First Quarto, appeared in 1600. The play follows four young Athenian lovers whose night in an enchanted forest is thrown into chaos by a fairy’s magic love potion.
tossups.r: That trickster, Puck, causes most of the trouble, including transforming a weaver named Nick Bottom so that he wears a donkey’s head. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy featuring the fairy monarchs Oberon and Titania.

tossups.p: This play’s six “rude mechanicals” include a tinker, a joiner, a bellows-mender, and a tailor. Led by Peter Quince, they rehearse a tragedy about Pyramus and Thisbe to perform at a royal wedding.
tossups.r: Their leading man, the weaver Nick Bottom, is given a donkey’s head by the trickster fairy Puck. In the nearby forest, four young Athenians are thrown into confusion by a magic love potion. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy featuring the fairy queen Titania.

tossups.p: In this play, a fairy’s mistake causes a young man named Lysander to abandon his beloved Hermia and fall instead for his rival’s former love, Helena. The fairy king Oberon eventually orders the mix-up corrected so that both Athenian couples can marry happily.
tossups.r: That same fairy, Puck, also transforms a weaver named Nick Bottom by giving him a donkey’s head while he rehearses a play with his fellow “rude mechanicals.” For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy that ends with a triple wedding presided over by Theseus.

tossups.p: This play opens with the Duke of Athens impatiently awaiting his wedding to Hippolyta, queen of the Amazons, in four days’ time. Their marriage celebration at the end of the play includes a disastrous performance of Pyramus and Thisbe.
tossups.r: That tragedy is performed by a troupe of “rude mechanicals” led by Peter Quince, whose star actor Nick Bottom spends much of the play wearing a donkey’s head. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy in which the fairy Puck confuses two pairs of young lovers with a magic potion.

tossups.p: This play’s mischievous sprite is also known as Robin Goodfellow, a trickster figure from English folklore. Acting on the fairy king Oberon’s orders, he smears the juice of a magic flower on a sleeping Athenian’s eyelids.
tossups.r: He means to fix Demetrius’s feelings for Helena but enchants Lysander instead, confusing both young men, and the same fairy later gives a weaver named Nick Bottom the head of a donkey. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy featuring the fairy queen Titania.

tossups.p: This play’s amateur actors choose to rehearse in the forest at night so curious townspeople will not discover their secret play. There, their leading man is transformed by a mischievous fairy into a creature with a donkey’s head.
tossups.r: That same fairy, Puck, had already confused two Athenian men into chasing the same woman with a magic love potion, and Nick Bottom, the transformed weaver, briefly becomes the object of the fairy queen Titania’s affection. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy that also features the fairy king Oberon.

clues.t: Four young Athenians — Hermia, Lysander, Helena, and Demetrius — get mixed up by a magic love potion
The “rude mechanicals,” led by Peter Quince, perform the tragedy of Pyramus and Thisbe at a wedding
Weaver Nick Bottom is given a donkey’s head by the trickster fairy Puck
The fairy king Oberon and fairy queen Titania rule over the forest
Set partly in an enchanted forest outside Athens, where fairies meddle in human love lives
Puck is also known by the folklore name Robin Goodfellow
Titania falls in love with donkey-headed Bottom after Oberon enchants her eyes
Puck mistakenly charms Lysander instead of Demetrius; once Oberon charms Demetrius too, both men chase Helena
The magic flower, struck by one of Cupid’s arrows, is called “love-in-idleness”
The play is framed by the wedding of Theseus, Duke of Athens, to Hippolyta, queen of the Amazons
Hermia’s father Egeus invokes Athenian law to force her to marry Demetrius instead of Lysander
Puck comments on the lovers’ confusion by saying, “Lord, what fools these mortals be!”
Puck boasts he can disguise himself as “a roasted crab” or a “three-foot stool” to play pranks
Theseus claims “the lunatic, the lover, and the poet are of imagination all compact”
Puck’s epilogue begins, “If we shadows have offended, think but this, and all is mended”
Puck brags, “I go, I go; look how I go, swifter than arrow from the Tartar’s bow”
During the mechanicals’ play, one actor breaks character to assure the audience his lion costume is not real
Under Athenian law, Hermia faces death or life in a convent if she will not marry Demetrius, as her father Egeus demands
Before the play begins, Demetrius had courted Helena before switching his affections to her friend Hermia
Titania’s fairy attendants are named Peaseblossom, Cobweb, and Mustardseed
Oberon wants to win a changeling Indian boy away from Titania’s care
Shakespeare likely wrote this comedy around 1595; its first printed text, called the First Quarto, appeared in 1600
The mechanicals rehearse in the forest at night so curious townspeople will not discover their secret play
The play ends with a triple wedding in Athens uniting Theseus and Hippolyta with both pairs of young lovers

trap.title: Not just “dreams”
trap.body: A few tossups are actually about the broader idea of dreams (quoting lines like Puck’s epilogue or Prospero’s “we are such stuff as dreams are made on” from _The Tempest_) and only accept this play’s title as one possible answer among several. If the clues list several unrelated works about dreaming before narrowing down, the judges may want the single word “dreams,” not this specific play.
trap.fix: Wait for a giveaway that names Shakespeare, Puck, Bottom, or the Athenian lovers by name — that confirms the real answer is this play, not the general topic of dreams.
trap.line: Real answer line: A Midsummer Night’s Dream (also accept it without “A”).
